behaviors.name: network_communication
behaviors.why: Establishes network connections which can be used for data exfiltration or command and control.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('socket.', 'requests.', 'urllib.', 'httpx.', 'aiohttp.', 'ftplib.', 'telnetlib.', 'smtplib.', 'poplib.', 'imaplib.'))

behaviors.name: network_data_reception
behaviors.why: Receives data over the network which may include sensitive information.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.endswith(('.recv', '.recvfrom', '.read'))

behaviors.name: dns_activity
behaviors.why: DNS queries can reveal information about the domains the application interacts with.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('socket.gethostbyname', 'socket.gethostbyaddr', 'socket.gethostname', 'socket.getfqdn', 'socket.getaddrinfo', 'dns.resolver.resolve'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_http
behaviors.why: HTTP requests can be used to exfiltrate data to external servers.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('requests.', 'urllib.request.urlopen', 'httpx.', 'aiohttp.ClientSession.get', 'aiohttp.ClientSession.post'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_socket
behaviors.why: Socket operations can be used to send data to remote hosts, potentially exfiltrating sensitive information.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('socket.socket.send', 'socket.socket.sendto'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_scp
behaviors.why: SCP commands can transfer files to remote servers, leading to data exfiltration.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SFTPClient.put', 'subprocess.run.scp'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_webhook
behaviors.why: Webhooks can be used to send data to external services, potentially exposing sensitive information.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('requests.post', 'httpx.post', 'aiohttp.ClientSession.post'))

behaviors.name: data_collection_stdin
behaviors.why: Reading from standard input can expose sensitive user input or credentials.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('sys.stdin.read', 'input'))

behaviors.name: lateral_movement_ssh
behaviors.why: SSH commands can be used to move laterally within a network, compromising additional systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SSHClient.connect', 'subprocess.run.ssh'))

behaviors.name: self_propagation_scp
behaviors.why: Using SCP to copy files can facilitate the self-propagation of malware or malicious scripts.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SFTPClient.put', 'subprocess.run.scp'))

behaviors.name: fs_read
behaviors.why: Reading files can expose sensitive data stored on the filesystem.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('open', 'os.open', 'pathlib.Path.read_text', 'pathlib.Path.read_bytes'))

behaviors.name: fs_write
behaviors.why: Writing files can lead to unauthorized modifications or the creation of malicious files.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('open', 'os.open', 'pathlib.Path.write_text', 'pathlib.Path.write_bytes'))

behaviors.name: payload_dumping
behaviors.why: Dumping payloads can expose sensitive data or malicious code.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('pickle.dump', 'json.dump', 'yaml.dump'))

behaviors.name: fs_enum
behaviors.why: Enumerating filesystems can reveal sensitive directories and files.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('os.listdir', 'os.scandir', 'glob.glob', 'pathlib.Path.iterdir'))

behaviors.name: credential_access_bruteforce
behaviors.why: Brute force attacks on credentials can compromise system security.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('requests.post', 'httpx.post', 'aiohttp.ClientSession.post', 'paramiko.SSHClient.connect'))

behaviors.name: credential_access
behaviors.why: Accessing credentials can lead to unauthorized access to systems and data.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('getpass.getpass', 'os.environ.get', 'configparser.ConfigParser.get'))

behaviors.name: command_execution
behaviors.why: Executing arbitrary commands can lead to system compromise and data loss.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('os.system', 'subprocess.run', 'subprocess.Popen', 'subprocess.call'))

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_exec
behaviors.why: Executing dynamic code can introduce security vulnerabilities and allow for code injection.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('eval', 'exec'))

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_load
behaviors.why: Loading dynamic code can introduce security vulnerabilities and allow for code injection.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('importlib.import_module', 'importlib.util.spec_from_file_location', 'importlib.util.module_from_spec'))

behaviors.name: reflection_abuse
behaviors.why: Reflection abuse can lead to unauthorized access to internal components and methods, potentially bypassing security checks.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('getattr', 'setattr', 'hasattr', 'dir'))

behaviors.name: crypto_activity
behaviors.why: Cryptographic operations may involve handling sensitive data, and improper use can lead to vulnerabilities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('cryptography.', 'Crypto.', 'hashlib.', 'ssl.'))

behaviors.name: deobfuscation
behaviors.why: Deobfuscation techniques can reveal hidden malicious code, which is often used in malware analysis.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('base64.b64decode', 'zlib.decompress', 'binascii.unhexlify'))

behaviors.name: obfuscation_dynamic_config
behaviors.why: Dynamic configuration obfuscation can hide the true intent of the program, making it harder to detect malicious behavior.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('__import__', 'exec', 'eval', 'compile'))

behaviors.name: system_recon
behaviors.why: System reconnaissance can gather information about the environment, which can be used for privilege escalation or persistence.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('platform.', 'os.', 'sys.', 'psutil.'))

behaviors.name: process_recon
behaviors.why: Process reconnaissance can identify running processes, which can be used to evade detection or manipulate other processes.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('psutil.process_iter', 'os.popen', 'subprocess.Popen'))

behaviors.name: permission_manipulation
behaviors.why: Permission manipulation can change file or system permissions, leading to unauthorized access or privilege escalation.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('os.chmod', 'os.chown', 'os.setgid', 'os.setuid'))

behaviors.name: defense_evasion_daemon
behaviors.why: Creating daemons can allow programs to run in the background, evading detection and performing malicious activities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('daemon.DaemonContext', 'multiprocessing.Process'))

behaviors.name: defense_evasion
behaviors.why: Defense evasion techniques aim to avoid detection by security systems, making malicious activities harder to trace.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('ctypes.windll.kernel32.SetWindowsHookExA', 'ctypes.windll.user32.RegisterHotKey'))

behaviors.name: defense_evasion_gui
behaviors.why: GUI-based defense evasion can manipulate user interfaces to hide malicious actions from the user.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('tkinter.Tk', 'PyQt5.QApplication', 'wx.App'))

behaviors.name: persistence_registry
behaviors.why: Modifying the registry can allow programs to persist across reboots, maintaining long-term access to the system.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('winreg.SetValueEx', 'winreg.CreateKey'))

behaviors.name: persistence_cron
behaviors.why: Adding cron jobs can ensure that a program runs at specific times, maintaining persistence on Unix-like systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('subprocess.call', 'os.system') and 'crontab' in n)

behaviors.name: keylogging
behaviors.why: Keylogging can capture user input, including sensitive information such as passwords and credit card details.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('pynput.keyboard.Listener', 'keyboard.hook', 'ctypes.windll.user32.GetKeyState'))

behaviors.name: user_input_prompt
behaviors.why: Prompting for user input can be used to gather sensitive information or to interact with the user in a malicious way.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('input', 'tkinter.simpledialog.askstring', 'PyQt5.QtWidgets.QInputDialog.getText'))

behaviors.name: clipboard_abuse
behaviors.why: Abusing the clipboard can capture or modify copied data, leading to data theft or corruption.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('pyperclip.copy', 'pyperclip.paste', 'ctypes.windll.user32.OpenClipboard'))

behaviors.name: screenshot
behaviors.why: Taking screenshots can capture sensitive information displayed on the screen, leading to data theft.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('PIL.ImageGrab.grab', 'mss.mss().shot', 'ctypes.windll.user32.PrintWindow'))

behaviors.name: gui_abuse
behaviors.why: Abusing GUI elements can manipulate the user interface to perform actions without user consent or to deceive the user.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('tkinter.Button', 'PyQt5.QtWidgets.QPushButton', 'wx.Button'))

behaviors.name: install_hook
behaviors.why: Installing hooks can intercept system calls or events, allowing for monitoring or manipulation of system behavior.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('ctypes.windll.kernel32.SetWindowsHookExW', 'ctypes.windll.user32.SetWinEventHook'))
